title: Playing piano 'professor' in Atlantic City bawdy houses
summary: Hired from the corner to play in white and Black brothels, he describes the screens, the acts and the tips in summer and the slump in winter.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: We're up there, see. Now, we used to come down there to play a little piano. So, in Atlantic City, the only way I could make a living, I used to, to eat and sleep, after trying to be a little pimp or something around there. See, was to stand on the corner of North Carolina and Baltic and, up North Carolina Avenue, going towards the beach, were the white bawdy houses. And going south from Arctic Avenue, Baltic Avenue, was the black bawdy houses, you see. Well, we used to stand on the corner, and when, if they got a red hot John came in there, they would come down and say, get a piano player, a professor. Say, get one of the professors. Now, that's one word that later on in life I didn't want nobody to call me a professor. When I got to be a professor, I didn't want nobody ever to call me. But, we use to stand on the corner, and we used to see some awful sights in those houses, you know? No use to me mention them, but I can tell you some pretty funny things happened.
You see, there was a screen around us, see? But the maid would know us. It was a colored maid, mostly. The maids were colored. The prostitutes were white, see. And

their only visitors were white people, see. So, they'd fixed the screen so that, you know the crack, they'd fixed the screen so that you could see through the crack. And sometimes we'd be playing and look and some awful things used to happen, see. So.

Yeah, sexual acts. But, you see so, they had to do everything sometimes. A fellow would come in there and bark like a dog. And they'd all run around smelling each other, like this. And such tricks like that, you know what I mean? Such things as --

Yeah, well we were supposed to keep the music going. And when they got through, they would say, 'Give the professor something.' Well, maybe he was slow, so some of these girls would reach into his pocket, and get some, 'Oh, come on, give him something.' And maybe the man would take out a dollar, or some change or something, and they'd grab it all and say, 'Here, take it professor.' You know what I mean? And so, we did very well for ourselves out there. You see, out in the summertime.

Now, when the winter come, it was a different story. You see what I mean, because there were things that would happen, that we were going, the people that supported these houses were all gone away, and some of the white bawdy houses
closed, see? Because Atlantic City, now, was the playground of the world. And from May to September it was good. Now...
